sections.title: Growth over 1, 3 and 5 years
sections.what: How fast your money grew each year on average, compared with the market index.

insights.headline: Ahead of its benchmark
insights.sentence: Over 5 years this fund grew 17.1% a year; the Sample 500 index grew 14.6%. That is 2.5% a year ahead.

insights.headline: Roughly in line with its benchmark
insights.sentence: Over 5 years this fund grew 22.5% a year; the Sample Midcap index grew 23.1%. That is about the same.

insights.headline: Well behind its benchmark
insights.sentence: Over 5 years this fund grew 11.8% a year; the Sample LargeMidcap index grew 15.4%. That is 3.6% a year behind.

insights.headline: Tracking its index closely
insights.sentence: This fund copies the Sample 50 index. Over 5 years it returned 13.4% a year against 13.6% for the index, a gap of 0.2%. That is normal for an index fund.
insights.fund: Sample Large Cap Index Fund D

insights.headline: Ahead of its benchmark
insights.sentence: Over the last year this fund returned 28.0%; the Sample 500 index returned 17.5%. That is 10.5 percentage points ahead. One year is a short time to judge a fund, so treat this lightly.

sections.title: Year by year
sections.what: How the fund did in each calendar year, and by how much it finished ahead of or behind the benchmark (its alpha).

insights.headline: Beat its benchmark in most years, by a clear margin
insights.sentence: In every one of the last 5 calendar years this fund beat the Sample 500 index. On average it finished 3.0 percentage points ahead of the benchmark each year (its margin over the benchmark, often called alpha). The widest gap was +5.0 points in 2024; the narrowest was +2.2 points in 2022.

insights.headline: Roughly level with its benchmark year by year
insights.sentence: In 3 of the last 5 calendar years this fund beat the Sample Midcap index. On average it finished 0.4 percentage points behind the benchmark each year (its margin over the benchmark, often called alpha). The widest gap was +0.9 points in 2025; the narrowest was −2.6 points in 2023.

insights.headline: Well behind its benchmark year by year
insights.sentence: This fund did not beat the Sample LargeMidcap index in any of the last 5 calendar years. On average it finished 6.2 percentage points behind the benchmark each year (its margin over the benchmark, often called alpha). It fell furthest behind in 2022 (−7.0 points) and came closest in 2021 (−6.0 points).
insights.fund: Sample Large & Mid Cap Fund C
insights.suggestion: Worth checking whether the weak years share a cause, such as one theme falling out of favour.

insights.headline: Beats its benchmark about half the time
insights.sentence: In 5 out of every 10 three-year periods, counting every possible start date, this fund did better than the Sample Midcap index.

insights.headline: Rarely beats its benchmark

sections.title: In rising and falling markets
sections.what: How much of the market's gains and losses this fund took part in.

insights.headline: Gains more, loses less
insights.sentence: Over 5 years, for every ₹100 the Sample 500 index gained in rising months, this fund gained ₹108. For every ₹100 it lost in falling months, this fund lost ₹88. That is the helpful mix: more of the gains and less of the losses.

insights.headline: Moves much like its benchmark
insights.sentence: Over 5 years, for every ₹100 the Sample Midcap index gained in rising months, this fund gained ₹99. For every ₹100 it lost in falling months, this fund lost ₹103. That is close to what the benchmark itself did, so the fund adds little in either direction.

insights.headline: Smaller gains and bigger falls
insights.sentence: Over 5 years, for every ₹100 the Sample LargeMidcap index gained in rising months, this fund gained ₹82. For every ₹100 it lost in falling months, this fund lost ₹112. That is the least helpful mix.
insights.fund: Sample Large & Mid Cap Fund C
insights.suggestion: Worth asking whether this mix of gains and falls is what you want from this fund.

insights.headline: Moves almost exactly with its index
insights.sentence: Over 5 years, for every ₹100 the Sample 50 index gained in rising months, this fund gained ₹100. For every ₹100 it lost in falling months, this fund lost ₹100. That is what an index fund should do.

insights.headline: Fell about as much as its benchmark

cagr.title: Returns, a year at a time (CAGR)
cagr.text: CAGR is the steady yearly growth rate that would turn your starting amount into the final amount. It smooths out the ups and downs so you can compare funds fairly. The benchmark is the market index the fund is measured against.

calendar.title: Calendar-year returns and margin (alpha)
calendar.text: How the fund did from 1 January to 31 December of each year. It shows whether the results came every year or from one or two big years. The margin (often called alpha) is simply the fund's return minus the benchmark's for that year: +3 means 3 percentage points ahead, -2 means 2 behind. It is not the regression-based alpha some websites show.

capture.title: Upside and downside capture
capture.text: Take all the months the market (the benchmark) went up. Upside capture is how much of that rise the fund delivered. Do the same for the falling months and you get downside capture. Above 100 means more than the market, below 100 means less. You want upside high and downside low.

quartile.title: Quartile ranking
quartile.text: Line up every fund in the same category from best to worst, then cut the line into four equal groups. Q1 is the best quarter and Q4 is the worst.

rolling_returns.title: Rolling returns
rolling_returns.text: Instead of checking one start date, we check every possible start date and look at the returns over each 3-year (or 5-year) stretch. It shows how consistent a fund is, not whether it got lucky with one date.

drawdown.title: Worst fall (drawdown)
drawdown.text: How far the value dropped from its highest point to its lowest before recovering. It answers: how bad did it get, and could I have lived with that?

ter.title: Fund charges (TER)
ter.text: The yearly fee the fund house takes out of your money, shown as a percentage. It is already deducted from the returns you see. We compare it with the median (middle) fee of funds in the same category and the same type of plan, direct with direct and regular with regular, so the comparison is like for like.

aum.title: Fund size (AUM)
aum.text: AUM is the total money all investors have put into the fund. Very small funds can be costlier to run and are sometimes merged or closed; very large ones can find it harder to trade freely.

manager.title: Fund manager
manager.text: The person or team that picks the fund's investments. A track record belongs to whoever managed the fund at the time, so a recent change means the past may say less about the future.

tracking.title: Tracking an index
tracking.text: An index fund simply copies an index. A small gap against the index is normal (mostly the fund's charges); a big gap deserves a look.

concentration.title: Concentration
concentration.text: How much of your money sits in one fund or one type of fund. The more concentrated, the more one bad patch affects the whole portfolio.

disclaimer: This report describes how your funds have behaved in the past using the data shown. Past performance does not guarantee future results. It is general information and observations to discuss, not personal investment advice or a recommendation to buy, sell or switch any fund. Please speak to a registered adviser before acting on it.
